brand.name: KafkaBoost
brand.sub: Keep your PC cool and fast
banner.admin: Administrator rights are needed to fix or change settings. Checking works without them.
windowsOnly.title: Windows only
windowsOnly.text: This section changes Windows settings, so it is not available on {os}. Dashboard basics, System analysis, Apps, Settings and Help work on every system.
dashboard.verdict.fail: The optimization is not fully in place
dashboard.vbsAllow: Allow "Fix it" to turn VBS/hypervisor off again (a security setting; breaks WSL2/Docker)
dashboard.tiles.needsAdmin: Run KafkaBoost as administrator to see live CPU temperature, clock and power. HWiNFO runs with administrator rights, and a normal app cannot read its sensors.
dashboard.tiles.noSharing: No live readings: HWiNFO is not sharing its sensors. Start it from the HWiNFO card below, or turn on Shared Memory Support in its settings.
dashboard.tiles.hwMissing: No live readings: HWiNFO is not on this PC. Use the HWiNFO card below to get it (you are shown what is downloaded and asked first).
dashboard.tiles.hwStopped: No live readings: HWiNFO is installed on this PC but not running. Start it here (sensors only) and the tiles fill in within a few seconds.
dashboard.tiles.hwStoppedIni: No live readings: HWiNFO is installed but not running, and Shared Memory Support is off in its HWiNFO64.INI, so it would share nothing. Tick the box to turn it on (a backup of the file is made first), then start it.
dashboard.tiles.hwNoSm: No live readings: HWiNFO is running, but Shared Memory Support is off in its settings, so it shares nothing. In HWiNFO open Settings and tick Shared Memory Support, or stop it from the HWiNFO card below and start it again from there.
dashboard.tiles.iniConsent: Turn on Shared Memory Support in HWiNFO's INI (a backup is made)
dashboard.tiles.error: The live readings could not be taken. They will be tried again in a moment.
dashboard.level.title: Optimization level
dashboard.level.loading: Reading the state of your tweaks…
dashboard.level.none: Nothing to measure yet: no recommended tweak is available on this PC.
dashboard.level.cpuNo: CPU thermal tuning: not in place
dashboard.level.cpuNa: CPU thermal tuning: not counted (it is made for the Core i9-14900HX)
dashboard.level.formula: How it is computed: ({active} active tweaks + {cpu} for the CPU tuning) ÷ ({total} recommended tweaks + {cpuItem} for the CPU tuning) = {percent}%. Only safe, recommended tweaks count; a partly applied tweak counts as not active. Nothing else is added.
dashboard.level.note: Apply recommended turns on only the safe tweaks, after creating a restore point.

analysis.title: Your computer
analysis.intro: A read-only look at what this PC is and whether the tuning can be applied. Nothing is changed here.
opt.title: Choose what to optimize
opt.intro: Every optimization is explained before it runs, backed up, and can be undone from Restore.
opt.cpu.title: CPU thermal tuning
opt.cpu.desc: Undervolt, boost caps and power limits through ThrottleStop, applied at every logon, so the CPU stops hitting 100 °C.
wizard.vbsCheckbox: Yes, disable VBS/hypervisor (required for the undervolt)
step.detect.title: Detect your hardware
step.detect.desc: Reads your operating system, CPU and laptop model. The tuning values are specific to the Intel Core i9-14900HX, so the app refuses to continue on any other CPU.
step.detect.c1: Nothing is changed in this step.
step.backup.title: Back up current settings
step.backup.desc: Saves a timestamped copy of ThrottleStop.ini so you can always return to where you started.
step.backup.c1: Creates ThrottleStop.ini.bak_<date> next to the ini (skipped on a fresh install).
step.get.title: Get ThrottleStop
step.get.desc: Uses the ThrottleStop you already have (the folder of your startup task, or one extracted in Downloads, Desktop or Documents). Otherwise it unpacks the zip (tested with 9.7.3) into the install folder: download it from TechPowerUp first and keep it in Downloads, or pick it manually.
step.get.c1: Extracts the zip to C:\Tools\ThrottleStop (or the folder you chose).
step.vbs.title: Turn off VBS / hypervisor
step.vbs.desc: ThrottleStop can only change CPU voltages while Windows virtualization-based security is off. This is a security setting, so it is your choice.
step.vbs.c1: bcdedit hypervisorlaunchtype off, VBS off, memory integrity off.
step.vbs.c2: Breaks WSL2 and Docker (WSL2) until you roll back.
step.vbs.c3: Needs a reboot to take effect.
step.apply.title: Apply the tuning
step.apply.desc: Writes the tested profile into ThrottleStop.ini.
step.apply.c1: Undervolt: -100 mV core and P-cache, -90 mV E-cache.
step.apply.c2: Boost caps: P-cores 47x (4.7 GHz), E-cores 36x (3.6 GHz).
step.apply.c3: Power limits: PL1 65 W / PL2 85 W.
step.task.title: Always-on startup
step.task.desc: Registers a Windows scheduled task so ThrottleStop starts at every logon and a 5-minute watchdog brings it back if it is closed. It never starts a second copy.
step.task.c1: Task "ThrottleStop_Autostart", highest privileges, no battery limits.
step.task.c2: Starts ThrottleStop now and remembers your Windows build for the Dashboard check.
step.verify.title: Verify
step.verify.desc: Compares the saved settings with the profile and checks that ThrottleStop, the task and the hypervisor setting are in the expected state.
step.verify.c1: Read-only. If VBS was just disabled, reboot first and run this again.
finish.title: All steps finished
finish.reboot: Reboot Windows once so the VBS change takes effect, then open this app again: the Dashboard will tell you whether everything is in place. After that, ThrottleStop starts by itself at every logon.
finish.ok: ThrottleStop starts by itself at every logon and the watchdog keeps it running. Open the Dashboard any time (for example after a Windows update) to check that the optimization is still in place.
restore.title: Undo everything
restore.intro: Put the PC back the way it was before the tuning.
restore.w1: Removes the always-on startup task (ThrottleStop stops being started for you).
restore.w2: Restores the newest ThrottleStop.ini.bak_* backup, undoing the undervolt, boost caps and power limits.
restore.w3: Optionally re-enables virtualization-based security so WSL2 and Docker work again (needs a reboot; the undervolt stops working).
restore.confirm: Remove the autostart task and restore the newest ThrottleStop.ini backup?
help.title: Questions
help.intro: Short answers. The full documentation has the details.
help.a1: Only ThrottleStop's profile (undervolt, boost caps, power limits), a startup task for ThrottleStop and, if you choose, the VBS/hypervisor setting. It does not touch game files.
help.a2: Every change is backed up and reversible from Restore. Still, changing CPU voltages can cause instability: this chip logged a corrected CPU error at −100 mV, so the app never goes deeper.
help.q3: Do I have to keep the app open?
help.a3: No. ThrottleStop starts at every logon and a 5-minute watchdog keeps it running. The app itself can stay in the system tray and re-check every few minutes.
help.q4: Why does it ask to turn VBS off?
help.a4: Windows blocks voltage changes while virtualization-based security is on. Turning it off is a security trade-off and breaks WSL2/Docker until you restore it.
help.q5: Will it work on my laptop?
help.a5: The CPU tuning values are specific to the Lenovo Legion 83DE with an i9-14900HX. On another CPU the app explains why it will not apply them.
settings.title: Preferences
settings.intro: How the app looks and behaves. Changes are saved automatically.
settings.autostart: Start with the system (hidden in the tray)
settings.autostart.hint: Windows: a scheduled task with administrator rights. macOS and Linux: a normal login item.
settings.startHwinfo.hint: Starts the HWiNFO that is already on this PC (sensors only, once, a few seconds after the app starts) so the Dashboard tiles fill in. Needs administrator rights, and only happens when HWiNFO is not running and its INI already has Shared Memory Support on; the INI is never changed for you here. Off by default.
settings.autoRecord.hint: Checks every 10 minutes whether a game is loading the CPU, records that session and stops when the load ends. It only reads sensors and never changes a setting. Needs HWiNFO sharing its sensors.
settings.closeToTray: Closing the window keeps the app running in the tray
settings.notifications: Notify me when the optimization breaks
settings.installDir.hint: Leave empty to find it automatically (startup task, Downloads, Desktop, Documents).
settings.checkDaily: Look for updates automatically (a lookup only; nothing is downloaded without your click)
settings.resetConfirm: Reset every setting to its default?
settings.adminNeeded: Changing this needs administrator rights. Restart the app as administrator.

tweak.power-plan-performance.title: High-performance power plan
tweak.power-plan-performance.desc: Switches Windows to the Ultimate/High performance plan so the CPU is not parked or slowed between loads. Uses more power and heat on battery or idle; revert restores your previous plan.
tweak.fast-startup-off.title: Turn Fast Startup off
tweak.fast-startup-off.desc: Fast Startup keeps parts of Windows hibernated, so "Shut down" is not a clean boot and some driver changes wait for a real restart. Off gives a clean boot every time.
tweak.background-apps-off.title: Stop apps running in the background
tweak.background-apps-off.desc: Applies the Windows policy that stops Store apps from running in the background, freeing CPU and memory for the game.
tweak.delivery-optimization-off.title: Turn Delivery Optimization off
tweak.delivery-optimization-off.desc: Stops Windows from sharing update files with other PCs over your connection. Updates still download normally from Microsoft.
tweak.startup-delay-off.title: Remove the startup-apps delay
tweak.startup-delay-off.desc: Windows waits a few seconds before launching your startup apps. This removes the wait so the desktop is ready sooner.
tweak.dynamic-tick-off.title: Turn Dynamic Tick off
tweak.dynamic-tick-off.desc: Dynamic Tick lets Windows space out its timer interrupts to save power. Turning it off forces a constant tick, which some say makes frame pacing steadier; others say it only increases idle power and heat with no real gain. Opinions differ and we have not measured a difference ourselves. Needs a restart to take effect, and to go away.
tweak.sysmain-off.title: Turn SysMain (Superfetch) off
tweak.sysmain-off.desc: SysMain preloads apps into memory. On a fast NVMe drive it adds little and can cause disk activity; off frees that. Apps may open a touch slower on slow disks.
tweak.hags-on.title: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling
tweak.hags-on.desc: Lets the GPU manage its own video memory scheduling. Helps some games and can hurt others; needs a restart and a recent graphics driver.
tweak.game-mode-on.title: Game Mode on
tweak.game-mode-on.desc: Windows Game Mode asks Windows to avoid background work such as driver installs and update restarts while a game is in the foreground.
tweak.game-dvr-off.title: Turn Game Bar capture (Game DVR) off
tweak.game-dvr-off.desc: Stops background recording of gameplay by the Xbox Game Bar. Removes a source of overhead if you do not use it to record.
tweak.mouse-accel-off.title: Mouse acceleration off
tweak.mouse-accel-off.desc: Turns off "Enhance pointer precision" so the cursor moves the same distance for the same hand movement. Aim becomes consistent.
tweak.sticky-keys-off.title: Stop Sticky Keys pop-ups
tweak.sticky-keys-off.desc: Disables the Shift-five-times, Filter Keys and Toggle Keys shortcuts that pop up and minimize a game by accident.
tweak.dns-cloudflare.title: Use Cloudflare DNS (1.1.1.1)
tweak.dns-cloudflare.desc: Sets 1.1.1.1 / 1.0.0.1 on your active network adapters. Can make name lookups faster; it does not lower in-game ping. Revert restores your previous DNS.
tweak.network-throttling-off.title: Network throttling index off
tweak.network-throttling-off.desc: Removes the multimedia network throttle Windows applies while media is playing. Mostly relevant if you stream and download at the same time.
tweak.advertising-id-off.title: Turn the advertising ID off
tweak.advertising-id-off.desc: Stops apps from using a per-user advertising identifier to personalize ads.
tweak.activity-history-off.title: Turn activity history off
tweak.activity-history-off.desc: Stops Windows from collecting and uploading your activity history (apps and files you opened).
tweak.bing-search-off.title: No web results in Start search
tweak.bing-search-off.desc: Search in the Start menu only looks at your PC, without sending what you type to Bing.
tweak.tips-suggestions-off.title: Turn tips and suggestions off
tweak.tips-suggestions-off.desc: Hides promoted apps, "suggested" content and tips in Start, Settings and the lock screen.
tweak.telemetry-min.title: Minimum diagnostic data
tweak.telemetry-min.desc: Sets the telemetry policy to the lowest level. Home and Pro editions still send the required minimum; only Enterprise can fully turn it off.
tweak.copilot-off.title: Turn Copilot off (policy)
tweak.copilot-off.desc: Applies the policy that hides Windows Copilot. Newer Windows builds may ignore this policy.
tweak.transparency-off.title: Transparency effects off
tweak.transparency-off.desc: Turns off the glass/transparency effects of Windows. Slightly less GPU work and a flatter look.
tweak.taskbar-left.title: Align the taskbar to the left
tweak.taskbar-left.desc: Moves the Windows 11 taskbar icons to the left, like Windows 10.
tweak.widgets-off.title: Hide the Widgets button
tweak.widgets-off.desc: Removes the Widgets button from the Windows 11 taskbar.
tweak.classic-context-menu.title: Classic right-click menu
tweak.classic-context-menu.desc: Shows the full Windows 10 style right-click menu directly, without "Show more options".
tweak.end-task-taskbar.title: "End task" in the taskbar menu
tweak.end-task-taskbar.desc: Adds an End task entry to the right-click menu of taskbar apps, handy for frozen games.
tweak.menu-delay-off.title: Remove the menu delay
tweak.menu-delay-off.desc: Menus open instantly instead of after a short pause.
tweak.file-extensions-on.title: Show file extensions
tweak.file-extensions-on.desc: Always shows the .exe, .txt, .zip part of file names, which helps you spot disguised files.
tweak.show-hidden-files.title: Show hidden files
tweak.show-hidden-files.desc: Shows hidden files and folders in File Explorer.
tweak.detailed-bsod.title: Detailed blue-screen information
tweak.detailed-bsod.desc: Shows the technical parameters on a crash screen, which makes crashes easier to diagnose.
tweak.defender-realtime-off.title: Turn Defender real-time protection off
tweak.defender-realtime-off.desc: Disables the live scanning of Microsoft Defender. Your PC is exposed to malware while it is off. Windows may refuse it when Tamper Protection is on, and that is not bypassed.
tweak.core-isolation-off.title: Turn core isolation (VBS) off
tweak.core-isolation-off.desc: Turns off virtualization-based security. Lowers protection against kernel attacks, and is needed for ThrottleStop voltage control on some PCs. Breaks WSL2 and Docker.

sensors.title: Sensors
sensors.intro: Temperatures, clocks, voltages, power, fans and load for the CPU, GPU, motherboard, memory and disks, read by LibreHardwareMonitor. This covers the readings of a monitor like HWMonitor. It does not measure DPC/ISR latency: for that you still need a tool such as LatencyMon.
sensors.get.title: Get sensor support
sensors.get.what: KafkaBoost reads the sensors with {name} {version} (open source, {license}). It is not bundled with the app: it is downloaded from its official GitHub release only when you click the button below.
sensors.get.details: The download is about {mb} MB from github.com. It must match the SHA-256 fingerprint pinned in the app, otherwise it is deleted and nothing is installed. Only the library files are unpacked, into {dir}, a folder only administrators can change; the zip is deleted afterwards.
sensors.get.unsigned: The library files are not digitally signed by their authors, so the pinned fingerprint is what shows they are the release that was checked.
sensors.get.consent: I agree to download LibreHardwareMonitor {version} from GitHub
sensors.get.needsAdmin: Installing needs administrator rights. Restart the app as administrator, then come back to this screen.
sensors.driver.title: About drivers, Windows Security and anti-cheat
sensors.driver.body: GPU, load and memory readings need no driver, and neither do disks and board sensors when the app runs as administrator. CPU temperature, clocks and power come from CPU registers, which LibreHardwareMonitor 0.9.x reads through the PawnIO driver. KafkaBoost does not install it; installing it is your own decision. Without it those CPU readings are shown as missing, never as zero. Kernel drivers of monitoring tools can upset the anti-cheat of some online games. We have not tested any anti-cheat, so check the game rules before installing such a driver. Windows Security did not flag the download on the PC where this was built, which is one machine and not a guarantee.
sensors.driver.license: Sensor library: LibreHardwareMonitor, Mozilla Public License 2.0. KafkaBoost redistributes none of it: the files come from the official release on your request.
sensors.copied: The snapshot (JSON) was copied to the clipboard.
sensors.updated: Updated {time} (about every 2 s while this screen is open)
sensors.demo: Demo data, not from this PC
sensors.legend: Min and Max are the lowest and highest readings this screen has seen since it was opened or reset. Temperature colors are generic and not specific to your chip or disk: warm from {warm} °C, hot from {hot} °C. Check the maker's limits for your parts.
sensors.notice.needsAdmin: The app is not running as administrator, so CPU, disk and board sensors may be missing. This is what could be read without it.
sensors.notice.noDriver: No CPU temperature, clock or power is shown: they need the PawnIO driver, which is not installed. They are missing, not zero. KafkaBoost does not install drivers.
msg.sensors.missing: Sensor support is not installed yet.
msg.sensors.getNeedsAdmin: Administrator rights are required to install the sensor library. Restart the app as administrator.
msg.sensors.hashMismatch: The download did not match the pinned SHA-256 fingerprint, so it was deleted and nothing was installed.
msg.sensors.getFailed: Could not get the sensor library. {detail}
msg.sensors.loadFailed: The sensor library could not be loaded. {detail}
msg.sensors.empty: No sensor returned a value on this PC.
msg.sensors.needsAdmin: Not running as administrator: showing only what can be read without it.
msg.sensors.noCpuTemp: No CPU temperature was reported: the PawnIO driver is probably not installed.
hwinfo.title: Live telemetry source (HWiNFO)
hwinfo.why: The live tiles above (CPU temperature, clock and power) read HWiNFO's shared memory. HWiNFO is optional and is not part of KafkaBoost: the app can fetch the official portable build for you, but only after you read what it is and agree.
hwinfo.status.missing: HWiNFO is not on this PC, so there is no live telemetry.
hwinfo.status.live: HWiNFO is running and sharing its sensors: the live tiles are fed.
hwinfo.status.runningNoSm: HWiNFO is running, but its shared memory is not readable, so the tiles stay hidden. Turn on shared memory in HWiNFO, or stop it here and start it again from this card.
hwinfo.status.stopped: HWiNFO is on this PC but not running.
hwinfo.source.existing: Using the copy that was already on this PC: {dir} (version {version}).

The file must contain HWiNFO64.exe with a valid digital signature from {signer}; otherwise it is deleted and nothing is installed. opt.cs2.title: Counter-Strike 2
opt.cs2.desc: Four small, optional and reversible extras for CS2. No promises about FPS: they are standard Windows and game settings.
opt.cs2.fact1: GPU preference for cs2.exe (Windows Graphics settings)
opt.cs2.fact2: autoexec.cfg with a backup and one-click restore
opt.cs2.fact3: cs2_video.txt tuning (resolution, refresh rate) with a backup and one-click restore
opt.cs2.fact4: Launch options to copy into Steam
cs2.title: Counter-Strike 2
cs2.intro: Settings that belong to Counter-Strike 2 only. Each one is optional, explained, and can be undone from this page.
cs2.honest.title: What this does and does not do
cs2.honest.1: Nothing here promises more FPS. If your stutter came from the CPU hitting its temperature limit, the CPU thermal tuning is what addresses it; these are small extras.
cs2.honest.2: These are standard Windows and game settings. The two game files KafkaBoost writes are autoexec.cfg and cs2_video.txt (both optional, and the old one is saved first). No other game file is patched and nothing is injected into the game.
cs2.honest.3: We did not test how VAC or any other anti-cheat reacts to these settings. They are normal Windows and Steam options, but that is not a guarantee.
cs2.honest.4: KafkaBoost never edits Steam's own configuration (localconfig.vdf). Launch options are only shown and copied for you to paste.
cs2.loc.title: Game location
cs2.loc.fromSteam: Found through Steam ({count} library folders checked).
cs2.loc.userPicked: This is the cs2.exe you chose.
cs2.loc.notFound: Counter-Strike 2 was not found through Steam. Choose cs2.exe yourself (usually steamapps\common\Counter-Strike Global Offensive\game\bin\win64\cs2.exe). The launch options below work without it.
cs2.loc.invalid: The cs2.exe you chose earlier is gone, so Steam was searched instead.
cs2.gpu.title: GPU preference (Windows Graphics settings)
cs2.gpu.desc: Tells Windows to run cs2.exe on the high-performance GPU. On a laptop with an integrated and a dedicated GPU this makes sure the game is not left on the wrong one. It is the same switch as Settings > System > Display > Graphics.
cs2.gpu.where: Stored for your user only (HKCU\Software\Microsoft\DirectX\UserGpuPreferences), no administrator rights needed. Putting it back restores exactly what was there before, or removes the entry if there was none.
cs2.cfg.title: autoexec.cfg
cs2.cfg.desc: A small file of console settings the game reads at start. Tick the lines you want. Every line is a suggestion you can edit in the file later. An existing autoexec.cfg is copied to autoexec.cfg.bak_<date and time> first.
cs2.cfg.opt.showfps: Shows the frame counter in a corner of the screen, so you can see stutter while you play. Compare it with the Sensors page.
cs2.cfg.opt.fpsmax: Frame-rate limit (the Video menu has the same setting). A limit your PC can hold steadily keeps CPU and GPU load, and so heat, lower. Enter your own number, {min} to {max}.
cs2.cfg.loadNote: CS2 is expected to run autoexec.cfg by itself when it starts, but KafkaBoost cannot check that from outside the game, so check it in game: if a line has no effect, open the console and type exec autoexec, or keep +exec autoexec in the launch options below.
cs2.cfg.confirmBody: KafkaBoost will write these lines to autoexec.cfg in the game's cfg folder. Nothing else in the game folder is touched.
cs2.cfg.confirmBackup: A file already exists there. It is copied to autoexec.cfg.bak_<date and time> first, and "Restore previous" puts it back.
cs2.cfg.confirmNoBackup: There is no autoexec.cfg yet, so there is nothing to back up. "Restore previous" will remove the file KafkaBoost writes.
cs2.cfg.restoreBody: The file written by KafkaBoost is replaced by your earlier autoexec.cfg from the backup, or removed if there was none. A file you changed yourself (without the KafkaBoost marker line) is never touched.
cs2.video.title: cs2_video.txt (resolution, refresh rate)
cs2.video.desc: The same resolution and refresh rate the in-game Video menu sets, written straight to the file Steam keeps for your account. You choose the numbers; nothing here is a recommendation. Only the keys you tick are touched, everything else already in the file (shadows, textures, anti-aliasing, ...) is left exactly as it was. The existing file is copied first.
cs2.video.opt.res-width: Horizontal resolution in pixels. Must be one your monitor actually supports, or the game may show the wrong thing until you fix it again in the Video menu. Enter your own number, {min} to {max}.
cs2.video.opt.res-height: Vertical resolution in pixels. Same rule as width: it has to be one your monitor actually supports. Enter your own number, {min} to {max}.
cs2.video.opt.refresh-rate: Refresh rate in Hz. Must match what your monitor and its cable/port actually support. Enter your own number, {min} to {max}.
cs2.video.confirmBody: KafkaBoost will update only the keys you ticked in cs2_video.txt for your signed-in Steam account. Nothing else in that file, or anywhere else in Steam, is touched.
cs2.video.confirmBackup: A file already exists there. It is copied to cs2_video.txt.bak_<date and time> first, and "Restore previous" puts it back.
cs2.video.confirmNoAccount: cs2_video.txt was not found, or no signed-in Steam account could be found. Start Counter-Strike 2 once, open the in-game Video settings, then try again.
cs2.video.restoreBody: The file written by KafkaBoost is replaced by your earlier cs2_video.txt from the backup, or removed if there was none. A file you changed yourself (without the KafkaBoost marker line) is never touched.
cs2.launch.title: Launch options
cs2.launch.desc: Tick what you want and copy the line into Steam. Options marked disputed or placebo are listed so you know what they are, not because we recommend them.
cs2.launch.opt.exec: Runs autoexec.cfg at start. Harmless if the game already does it, useful if it does not.
cs2.launch.opt.console: Opens the developer console at start, so you can type exec autoexec or check a setting.
cs2.launch.opt.high: Asks Windows to give the game process high priority. Opinions differ and nobody has shown a reliable gain; it can also starve other programs. Leave it off unless you test it yourself.
cs2.launch.opt.vulkan: Uses the Vulkan renderer instead of DirectX 11. It can be better or worse depending on your GPU and driver. Try it only if you will compare the result yourself.
cs2.launch.opt.novid: Meant to skip the intro video. Many guides still list it, but it is reported to do nothing in CS2.
cs2.launch.opt.nojoy: Turns off controller support. The memory it saves is tiny, and it only makes sense if you never use a controller.
cs2.launch.copied: Copied. Paste it into the Launch options box in Steam.
cs2.launch.copyFailed: Could not copy automatically. The text is selected: press Ctrl+C.
cs2.launch.where: Where to paste it: Steam > Library > right-click Counter-Strike 2 > Properties > General > Launch options (one line).
cs2.launch.noVdf: KafkaBoost does not edit Steam's files: Steam rewrites them and a wrong edit could corrupt them. You paste the line yourself.
msg.cs2.notFound: Counter-Strike 2 was not found through Steam.
msg.cs2.badExe: Choose the cs2.exe file (it has to exist).

msg.cs2.autoexecRestored: Your previous autoexec.cfg was put back (from {backup}).
msg.cs2.autoexecRemoved: There was no autoexec.cfg before, so the one KafkaBoost wrote was removed.
msg.cs2.autoexecNotOurs: The current autoexec.cfg was not written by KafkaBoost (or its marker line is gone), so it was left alone.
msg.cs2.noVideoAccount: No signed-in Steam account could be found, so cs2_video.txt is not available. Open Steam and sign in, then try again.
msg.cs2.noVideoFile: cs2_video.txt was not found. Start Counter-Strike 2 once and open the Video settings so it is created, then try again.
msg.cs2.videoWritten: cs2_video.txt updated. Your previous file was saved as {backup}.
msg.cs2.videoRestored: Your previous cs2_video.txt was put back.
msg.cs2.videoRemoved: There was no cs2_video.txt before, so the one KafkaBoost wrote was removed.
msg.cs2.videoNotOurs: The current cs2_video.txt was not written by KafkaBoost (or you removed our marker line), so it was left alone.
tweaks.pv.intro: These {count} tweaks will be changed on this PC. For each one you see what it does, what you may notice, and the exact Windows settings: the value now, the new value, and what turning it off puts back.
tweaks.pv.offDelete: turning it off: the value is deleted again
tweaks.pv.offValue: turning it off: set back to {value}
tweaks.pv.offKeyDelete: turning it off: the key is deleted again
tweaks.pv.offKeyKeep: turning it off: the key is kept (it was already there)
tweaks.pv.serviceStop: the service is also stopped now (it is running)
tweaks.pv.serviceMissing: Service {name}: not found on this PC
tweaks.pv.offService: turning it off: start type set back to {value}
tweaks.pv.plan: Active power plan: {current} → Ultimate Performance (High performance if that is not available)
tweaks.pv.offPlan: turning it off: {current} is activated again
tweaks.pv.dnsNone: No active network adapter was found
tweaks.pv.offDns: turning it off: set back to {value}
tweaks.pv.offDefender: turning it off: real-time protection is switched on again
tweaks.pv.offVbs: turning it off: it is enabled again (needs a restart)
tweaks.pv.offBcd: turning it off: the setting is put back as it was (needs a restart)
tweaks.pv.error: Could not read the current state: {detail}
tweaks.pv.adminNo: Administrator rights: not needed (your own user settings)
tweaks.pv.adminMissing: KafkaBoost is not running as administrator, so Windows will refuse this one.
tweaks.pv.rebootYes: Restart: needed for it to take effect
tweaks.pv.unavailable: The current values could not be read, so only the names are shown. Nothing else is different: only these tweaks are applied.
tweaks.pv.closing: First, KafkaBoost tries to create a Windows restore point (Windows allows one every 24 hours; if Windows declines, the tweaks still apply). Nothing is installed and nothing is deleted: only the values listed above are written.
tweaks.pv.closing2: Each tweak can be turned off again in Optimizations, and the previous values are restored. Advanced and risky tweaks are never part of this.
tweak.fast-startup-off.notice: Shut down takes a little longer and the next start is a full boot. Restart is unchanged.
tweak.background-apps-off.notice: Store apps (for example Mail or Weather) stop refreshing and sending notifications while closed. Normal desktop programs are not affected.
tweak.delivery-optimization-off.notice: Nothing visible. Updates and Store downloads come only from Microsoft.
tweak.startup-delay-off.notice: Your startup apps open right at sign-in, so the desktop can feel busy for the first moments.
tweak.game-mode-on.notice: Nothing visible. Windows may hold back update restarts and driver installs while a game is in front.
tweak.game-dvr-off.notice: Background recording and clip capture of the Game Bar stop working. Turn this off again if you record gameplay with it.
tweak.mouse-accel-off.notice: The pointer feels different at first: the same hand movement always moves it the same distance. It can take a little time to get used to.
tweak.sticky-keys-off.notice: Pressing Shift five times no longer opens the Sticky Keys prompt. If you rely on these accessibility features, leave this off.
tweak.advertising-id-off.notice: You still see ads, just not tailored with the advertising ID.
tweak.activity-history-off.notice: Features that use that history, such as picking up recent activity on another device, stop working.
tweak.bing-search-off.notice: Start search shows only results from your PC; web suggestions disappear.
tweak.tips-suggestions-off.notice: Fewer promoted apps and tips in Start, Settings and the lock screen.

dashboard.session.title: Play session
dashboard.session.intro: Records temperature, clocks and power while you play, then shows a summary. It only reads the sensors; nothing in your settings is changed.
dashboard.session.note: Needs HWiNFO sharing its sensors. It keeps recording while the window is hidden in the tray.
dashboard.session.limits: Readings at PL1 ({pl1} W) / PL2 ({pl2} W)
dashboard.session.whea19: WHEA 19 (internal parity error) logged, {count} event(s). Do not deepen the undervolt; use -80/-80/-70 mV.
dashboard.session.noFlags: These sensors do not report throttle flags, so this summary does not say whether the CPU throttled.
msg.session.noSensors: No live readings: HWiNFO is not sharing its sensors, so there is nothing to record.
dashboard.advice.title: Boost clock advice
dashboard.advice.intro: Looks at your recorded play sessions and says whether the P-core cap has measured room for one more step. It only advises: nothing is changed for you.
dashboard.advice.note: Uses your last recorded sessions. Try a suggestion with two matched runs before keeping it.
dashboard.advice.notEnough.fewSessions: Not enough data yet: {loaded} of {needed} loaded sessions recorded (5 minutes or more under real load). Record a few play sessions first.
dashboard.advice.notEnough.noSensors: Not enough data: the recorded sessions are missing temperature, clock or power readings.
dashboard.advice.notEnough.noCap: The boost cap could not be read from the tuning settings.
dashboard.advice.hold.whea: Keep {cap}x. A WHEA event was logged during a recorded session, so do not raise anything now.
dashboard.advice.hold.hot: Keep {cap}x. A recorded session reached {temp} °C, so there is no thermal room.
dashboard.advice.hold.marginal: Keep {cap}x. The hottest session reached {temp} °C: too close to the limit to add clock.
dashboard.advice.hold.notCapBound: Keep {cap}x. Your games did not reach the cap (highest {clock} MHz), so raising it would change nothing.
dashboard.advice.hold.powerBound: Keep {cap}x. The CPU was held at its power limit during your sessions, so a higher cap would need more watts, not just clock.
dashboard.advice.raise.headroom: There may be room for {next}x (one step above {cap}x): {loaded} loaded sessions peaked at {temp} °C, reached the cap, stayed under the power limit and logged no WHEA. This is a suggestion, not a promise of stability: change it yourself and confirm with two matched runs.
dashboard.advice.lowerCheck.whea19: Do not raise the clock. WHEA 19 (internal parity error) was logged. If it returns, use the -80/-80/-70 mV undervolt.
dashboard.advice.evidence: {loaded} loaded sessions · highest temperature {temp} °C · highest P-core clock {clock} MHz · average power {power} W
dashboard.advice.failed: The advice could not be computed.
insights.title: Insights
insights.intro: Record a play session and see what your PC did: temperatures, clocks, power and WHEA. Then ask whether the boost clock has measured room. Everything here only reads sensors.
opt.rammap.title: Memory cleanup (RAMMap)
opt.rammap.desc: Runs Microsoft's RAMMap on demand to empty parts of Windows memory, and measures what changed. Manual, optional and reversible (memory refills by itself).
opt.rammap.fact1: Downloaded from Microsoft only after you agree, and its signature is checked
opt.rammap.fact2: Five actions, one click each, nothing automatic
opt.rammap.fact3: Memory counters before and after every run, with a history
rammap.title: Memory cleanup (RAMMap)
rammap.intro: RAMMap is a Microsoft Sysinternals tool. KafkaBoost runs one of its "empty" actions when you ask, then reads the Windows memory counters before and after so you can see what actually changed.
rammap.honest.title: What to expect
rammap.honest.1: We do not promise more FPS. Whether Counter-Strike 2 slowly fills memory, and whether emptying it helps, is disputed, and we have not measured a gain.
rammap.honest.2: Emptying the standby list throws away cached data. Windows has to read it from the disk again, so the game can stutter for a moment right after.
rammap.honest.3: The numbers below are the Windows counters we read ourselves. A counter Windows does not report is shown as a dash, never as 0.
rammap.get.title: Get RAMMap
rammap.get.text: RAMMap is not on this PC. It is downloaded from {source}, must carry a valid digital signature from {signer}, and is kept in a folder only administrators can change. It is proprietary freeware ({license}); it is not part of KafkaBoost and is not redistributed by it.
rammap.get.agree: I agree to download RAMMap from Microsoft
rammap.mem.title: Memory now
rammap.mem.note: Standby is cached data Windows can drop at any time; modified is data waiting to be written to disk.
rammap.badSignature: RAMMap64.exe on this PC does not have a valid Microsoft signature, so it will not be started. Remove it and download it again.
rammap.actions.title: Actions
rammap.action.working-sets.title: Empty working sets
rammap.action.working-sets.desc: Asks every program to give back memory it is not using right now. Programs may be a little slower for a moment while they take it back.
rammap.action.system-working-sets.title: Empty system working sets
rammap.action.system-working-sets.desc: Does the same for Windows itself and its drivers.
rammap.action.modified-pages.title: Empty modified page list
rammap.action.modified-pages.desc: Writes data waiting in memory out to the disk so the memory can be reused. Causes a burst of disk writes.
rammap.action.standby-low.title: Empty low-priority standby list
rammap.action.standby-low.desc: Drops only the lowest-priority cached data. The gentlest way to free cache.
rammap.action.standby.title: Empty standby list
rammap.action.standby.desc: Drops all cached data. Frees the most memory, but the game and Windows must read it back from the disk, which can cause stutter.
rammap.confirm.safe: This only asks programs to give memory back. You can run it again at any time.
rammap.confirm.advanced: Windows can refill this by itself, so nothing is lost, but the next few seconds may be slower while data is read again.
rammap.confirm.noPromise: KafkaBoost does not promise a performance gain. It will show you what the memory counters did.
rammap.history.title: History
rammap.history.totals: {runs} run(s). Standby memory released in the {measured} run(s) where it was measured: {released}.
msg.rammap.needsAdmin: Administrator rights are required for this. Restart the app as administrator.
msg.rammap.state.missing: RAMMap is not on this PC.
msg.rammap.notInstalled: RAMMap is not on this PC yet.
msg.rammap.badSignature: RAMMap64.exe does not have a valid digital signature from Microsoft Corporation (status {status}, signer "{signer}"). It was not started or installed.
msg.rammap.alreadyRunning: RAMMap is already running. Close it first.
msg.rammap.unknownAction: That RAMMap action does not exist.
msg.rammap.badZip: The download was not a zip with RAMMap64.exe. Nothing was installed.
msg.rammap.badSource: The download address is not from the expected Microsoft site. Nothing was downloaded.
memory.title: Memory
memory.intro: The Windows memory counters, live. Nothing here changes your PC: it only reads what Windows reports, every 2 seconds, while this page is open.
memory.live.title: Right now
memory.bar.label: Installed memory split into in use, modified, standby and free
memory.note: Available = free + standby. Standby is cached data Windows can drop at any time, so a large standby is normal. Modified is data waiting to be written to disk. A counter Windows does not report is shown as a dash.
dashboard.session.memNote: Free memory that stays very low while the game runs points to memory pressure. A large standby is normal: it is cache Windows can drop at any time. This only shows what Windows reported; it does not say a cleanup would help.
